chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought a man who had sold a free person, so he cut his hand.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.حُرّاً: A free person (as opposed to a slave)
key_terms.فَقَطَعَ يَدَهُ: So he cut his hand (the specific legal punishment)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for selling a free person in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) application of the hadd punishment for theft (qat’ al-yad) to the crime of kidnapping and selling a free person, a ruling that highlights the juristic debate regarding whether this penalty applies to the seller, the buyer, or both. It reflects the early Shia and Sunni legal tradition of extending established penal codes to new economic crimes involving the commodification of human liberty. The narration underscores the gravity of treating a free human as a chattel, linking it directly to the Quranic concept of theft (sariqa).
